questions.subject: English Language
questions.question: Either the driver or the passengers _______ expected to report the incident at the station.
questions.explanation: With 'either... or', the verb agrees with the closer subject ('passengers', plural), requiring the plural verb 'are'.
questions.explanation_short: Plural verb 'are' agrees with closer plural noun 'passengers'.
questions.explanation_pidgin: Look the word wey near the gap pass: 'passengers' na plenty people, so na 'are' we go use.

questions.subject: English Language
questions.question: Choose the option nearest in meaning to the word in italics: The referee ignored the player's *blatant* foul.
questions.explanation: 'Blatant' means very obvious and done openly without shame.
questions.explanation_pidgin: 'Blatant' mean say everybody see am clear-clear, so 'obvious' na the answer.
